Introduction to Hampden Probate and Family Court

The Hampden Probate and Family Court serves as the primary legal resource for residents of Hampden County, Massachusetts dealing with family matters, probate issues, and related legal concerns. This comprehensive guide covers everything from accessing services to navigating the court's resources both in-person and online.

Getting to the Court

Parking Options

Multiple paid parking garages are located near the courthouse, along with metered street parking. This variety ensures convenient access regardless of your transportation preferences.

Public Transportation

The court is accessible via several Pioneer Valley Transit Authority routes, including:

  • Blue 6 and 7
  • Green 1, 2, 5, and 8

These routes make the courthouse easily accessible for those who prefer not to drive.

Court Services

In-Person Services

The Hampden Probate and Family Court offers comprehensive assistance for various legal matters, including:

  • Family law cases
  • Probate proceedings
  • Estate administration
  • Guardianships and conservatorships

Digital Services

The court has embraced technology to make legal processes more accessible:

  • Virtual Registry Assistance: Get help with court-related matters remotely
  • eFiling System: Submit documents electronically to save time and paper
  • eReminder Notifications: Stay updated about upcoming court dates and deadlines

Online Resources

Court Case Records

  • View case record information at public access computers and courthouses
  • Search Superior, District, Probate and Family, Housing, Land, and Boston Municipal Court case records online
  • Access the court's digital records database

Forms and Documentation

  • Download court forms organized by topic or department
  • Access legal templates not filed in court (tax forms, contracts, wills, etc.)
  • Find Massachusetts Trial Court Law Library resources

Self-Help Resources

The court provides extensive self-help materials for those navigating the legal system without an attorney:

  • Elder abuse resources
  • Domestic violence assistance
  • Victim/witness support services
  • Information on specialty court sessions
  • Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) guidance
  • Child support services (applications, payments, modifications)
  • Self-representation guidance for civil cases
  • Fee waiver request information
  • Legal terminology glossary

Law Libraries and Legal Research

Massachusetts Trial Court Law Libraries offer:

  • Extensive legal materials and services
  • "Ask a Law Librarian" assistance
  • Multilingual legal information
  • Self-help resources

  • Directory of free/low-cost legal service organizations

FAQs

How can I access court case records online?
You can search case records through the court's website using the online records search system.

What resources are available for self-representation?
The court provides comprehensive guidance materials, forms, and procedural information for self-represented litigants.

How do I file a complaint against an attorney?
Complaints can be filed through the Massachusetts Board of Bar Overseers, with information available through the court.

What services does the Community Legal Services and Counseling Center provide?
This organization offers integrated legal assistance and mental health counseling services.

How can I find an attorney in Massachusetts?
Use the Lawyer Directory provided by the Board of Bar Overseers to search by name, bar number, or location.

How do I access the virtual registry?
Visit the court's website or contact the court office directly for virtual registry access instructions.

What types of cases does this court handle?
The court handles family law matters, probate proceedings, estate administration, guardianships, and related legal issues.

Are there fees for court services?
Yes, filing fees apply to many services. Contact the court directly for specific fee information, and ask about fee waiver options if needed.

Can I file documents electronically?
Yes, the court's eFiling system allows electronic document submission for most case types.

Is the court accessible by public transportation?
Yes, multiple Pioneer Valley Transit Authority routes serve the courthouse location
